profile.summary: GENERator is a family of generative DNA language models that read DNA as six-base tokens and predict what comes next, like a text language model. The models handle long inputs (16,384 tokens, given as 98k base pairs in the first release) and are used to generate DNA sequences, score the effect of variants, and provide embeddings for classification tasks. The first release was trained on 386 billion nucleotides of eukaryotic DNA from RefSeq; the v2 series adds new eukaryote models and prokaryote models, at 1.2B and 3B parameters.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper Figure 1 caption, Section 4; v1 card; README

summary_quotes.text: GENERator is a generative DNA language model based on a transformer decoder architecture with 6-mer tokenization
The model is pre-trained on 386 billion nucleotides of eukaryotic DNA curated from the RefSeq database
With a maximum sequence length of 16,384 tokens
featuring a context length of 98k base pairs

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: GENERator is a decoder-only transformer, built on the LLaMA framework, that predicts the next 6-mer token of a DNA sequence. Grouping six bases per token lets a 16,384-token window cover long stretches of DNA. The authors compared tokenizers for this autoregressive setting and found 6-mers best, with BPE close to random on their sequence recovery test. For the first release they trained only on gene-centric regions of eukaryotic RefSeq genomes rather than whole genomes, which gave lower loss for the whole-genome model but better downstream results for the gene-centric one. Training sequences start at a random offset of 0 to 5 bases so the model sees different 6-mer framings.

quotes.text: GENERator adopts a decoder-only transformer architecture based on the LLaMA framework
With a maximum sequence length of 16,384 tokens
the 6-mer tokenizer emerges as the most effective configuration
Empirically, all-sequence training achieves a lower pre-training loss
whereas functional sequence training consistently yields superior performance across downstream tasks
we randomize the starting offset of each training sequence uniformly between 0 and 5 nucleotides

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: There are two generations. The first release (February 2025) has eukaryote models at 1.2B and 3B parameters. The v2 series (November 2025) adds new eukaryote models and prokaryote models at the same two sizes, described in a separate technical report on bioRxiv. The 1.2B configurations of the first release and v2 are identical; the v2 card adds a per-base sequence scoring function. The README asks users of the prokaryote models to re-download weights updated on 2026-07-06. A result should name the full checkpoint name, including v2 and eukaryote or prokaryote, and its Hugging Face revision. This page read GENERator-v2-eukaryote-1.2b-base at revision c41b0018 and GENERator-eukaryote-1.2b-base at revision 5e872c94. The paper gives the 1B model's pretraining compute as 11,776 A100-hours (368 hours on 32 GPUs) in Appendix B and as 11,793 A100-hours in its resource table (Table S16); the two figures conflict and the paper does not explain the difference. Table S16 gives 29,625 A100-hours for the 3B model.
sections.source_locator: README: News; v2 model card; paper Appendix B

quotes.text: GENERator-v2 technical report is now available on [bioRxiv]

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Generative DNA language model family (autoregressive transformer decoder) used for sequence generation, variant effect scoring and as a source of embeddings for fine-tuning.
facts.source_locator: Paper Figure 1 caption; v2 model card: How to use

quotes.text: GENERator is a generative DNA language model based on a transformer decoder architecture with 6-mer tokenization, pretrained using an autoregressive next-token prediction objective

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Decoder-only transformer based on the LLaMA framework with a 6-mer tokenizer. The 1.2B configuration (first release and v2 are identical): 26 layers, hidden size 2048, intermediate size 5632, 32 attention heads with 4 key-value heads, vocabulary 4128, RoPE theta 500000. The 3B configurations have 30 layers and hidden size 3072. The paper's Table S12 gives the same figures (26 and 30 layers, hidden size 2048 and 3072, 32 heads with 4 KV heads).
facts.source_locator: Paper Section 4.3 and Table S12; config.json files

quotes.text: GENERator adopts a decoder-only transformer architecture based on the LLaMA framework

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: DNA sequences, tokenised into 6-mers. For generation the input length should be a multiple of 6, by left padding with A or left truncation; otherwise an out-of-vocabulary token is appended. The v2 scoring function accepts any length.
facts.source_locator: README: Important Notice; v2 model card Example 3

quotes.text: please ensure that the length of each input sequence is a multiple of **6**
the tokenizer will append an `'<oov>'` (out-of-vocabulary) token to the end of the token sequence
# Sequence length does not need to be a multiple of 6

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Generated DNA continuations; hidden-state embeddings (separator token, last DNA token or mean pooling); and, in v2, per-base probabilities of A, T, C and G from model.score_sequence, which can be turned into sequence log-likelihoods.

quotes.text: # Option 3: Mean pooling over all tokens
# bp_probs[i] = [P(A), P(T), P(C), P(G)] at position i (i ranges 0 ... len(seq)-1)

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: 1,162,061,824 (each 1.2B checkpoint) and 2,998,262,784 (each 3B checkpoint), from the Hugging Face safetensors counts of all six base models.
facts.source_locator: Hugging Face API safetensors field for each checkpoint

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: DNA from the RefSeq database. The first-release eukaryote models were trained on a gene-centric functional corpus of 386 billion nucleotides from all eukaryotic organisms in RefSeq (gene loci with exons, introns, UTRs and nearby regulatory regions). The README lists 422B for the v2 eukaryote models and 515B for the v2 prokaryote models; the v2 data are not described further in the sources read.

quotes.text: we sourced genomic DNA sequences from all eukaryotic organisms available in the RefSeq database
The resulting functional corpus contains a total of 386 billion nucleotides.

facts.label: Known versions
facts.value: Six base checkpoints: first release GENERator-eukaryote-1.2b-base and -3b-base; v2 GENERator-v2-eukaryote-1.2b-base and -3b-base; and v2 GENERator-v2-prokaryote-1.2b-base and -3b-base. The README notes an important update to the prokaryote weights on 2026-07-06. The same account also publishes GENERanno annotation models, not covered here.
facts.source_locator: README: model table, News; GenerTeam model listing

quotes.text: **[2025-11-05]** GENERator-v2 series are now available on [HuggingFace](https://huggingface.co/GenerTeam/)!

facts.label: Training cutoff
facts.value: Not reported. The sources read do not date the RefSeq download.

facts.label: Context limits
facts.value: 16,384 tokens (6-mers), the maximum sequence length in pretraining and max_position_embeddings in the config.json of all six checkpoints. The paper's Table S12 lists a context length of 16,384 (98,304 bp) for both sizes. The first-release card describes this as a context length of 98k base pairs. The README says sliding-window attention extended the context to 1 million bp on one A100 GPU.

strengths.text: Long context for a transformer: 16,384 6-mer tokens, which the first-release card gives as 98k base pairs.

quotes.text: featuring a context length of 98k base pairs

strengths.text: Fast generation by the authors' measurement: tens of times faster than Evo2 at comparable sizes on one L40S GPU.

quotes.text: GENERator exhibits tens-fold faster generation speed compared to Evo2 across model sizes

strengths.text: Code and weights are MIT licensed and not gated, and the repository has scripts for variant effect prediction, sequence recovery, classification and fine-tuning.
Separate eukaryote and prokaryote models in v2, so users can match the model to their organisms.

limitations.text: The 6-mer tokenizer means generation inputs must be a multiple of 6 bases long, or the output can degrade into repeats such as AAAAAA.

quotes.text: please ensure that the length of each input sequence is a multiple of **6**
This can result in uninformative subsequent generations, such as repeated `'AAAAAA'`.

limitations.text: The card examples need a CUDA GPU and FlashAttention 2, and the models have 1.2 to 3 billion parameters. Inference memory needs are not stated.
The first-release models were trained on gene-centric regions of eukaryotic genomes only; the v2 training data and methods are described in a bioRxiv report that was not read here.

quotes.text: In this setting, we construct a gene-centric pre-training corpus based on RefSeq annotations.
More technical details are provided in the GENERator-v2 [technical report]

run_guide.summary: Install the repository's requirements at a pinned commit and generate 32 tokens of continuation for two DNA sequences with GENERator-v2-eukaryote-1.2b-base.
prerequisites: Python 3.10, as the README states, and a CUDA GPU; the card example uses FlashAttention 2 and bfloat16. GPU memory needs are not stated.
Internet access to download the weights from Hugging Face (not gated). The README suggests the mirror https://hf-mirror.com if huggingface.co is unreachable.
Code and weights are MIT licensed.

steps.title: Get the code and install requirements
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/GenerTeam/GENERator.git
cd GENERator
git checkout --detach 5132e2c35da5d5e9a7dcec7484901be4de864bf6
pip install -r requirements.txt
pip install flash-attn --no-build-isolation
steps.explanation: The README's dependency steps with a checkout line added to pin the commit this page read. The README lists FlashAttention as recommended for long sequences; it is installed here because the card example requests flash_attention_2.

steps.title: Generate sequences
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
import torch
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForCausalLM

model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    "GenerTeam/GENERator-v2-eukaryote-1.2b-base",
    attn_implementation="flash_attention_2",
    trust_remote_code=True,
    dtype=torch.bfloat16,
).cuda().eval()

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(
    "GenerTeam/GENERator-v2-eukaryote-1.2b-base",
    trust_remote_code=True,
)

# Define input sequences.
sequences = [
    "ATCGATCGATCGATCGATCGATCGATCGATCGATCGATCGATCGATCGATCGATCGATCG",
    "ACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGTACGT"
]

# Truncate each sequence to the nearest multiple of 6
processed_sequences = ["<s>" + seq[len(seq)%6:] for seq in sequences]

# Tokenize the sequences
inputs = tokenizer(
    processed_sequences,
    add_special_tokens=False,
    return_tensors="pt",
    padding=True,
    padding_side="left",
).to("cuda")

# Generate the sequences
with torch.inference_mode():
    outputs = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=32, do_sample=False)

# Decode the generated sequences
decoded_sequences = tokenizer.batch_decode(outputs, skip_special_tokens=True)

# Print the decoded sequences
print(decoded_sequences)
PY
steps.explanation: Example 1 from the v2 model card, unchanged, wrapped in a shell heredoc.

quotes.text: processed_sequences = ["<s>" + seq[len(seq)%6:] for seq in sequences]

outputs: A list of the two input sequences followed by their generated continuations, printed to the terminal.
